title: Which of the queen's lockers stay open at the end?
description: A queen leaves a will with a puzzle: one hundred closed lockers in a secret room, and one hundred people who each toggle some of them. The video shows the first few people at work and stops on the question of which lockers end open.
teaching_notes: One idea: a simple rule repeated many times can leave a surprising pattern. Collect guesses about which lockers stay open and confirm none, because the chapter settles it by counting factors. Watch for students who think every locker ends the same way.

source: A hundred lockers and a hidden treasure
video_script.why: Before any square number is named, the child meets the puzzle that drives the chapter: which lockers end open after a hundred people have toggled them.
video_script.substitution: Picture a long row of closed doors, and a line of people who each flip some of the doors in turn.
video_script.anchor: the secret room of Ruhee's mansion with a hundred closed lockers

names.Ruhee: the queen of Khoisnam whose will hides the treasure in one of 100 lockers

maths_rules: There are 100 lockers, all closed at the start, and 100 people.
Person 1 opens every locker, person 2 toggles every 2nd locker, person 3 every 3rd locker, and so on to person 100.
To toggle a locker means to close it if it is open and to open it if it is closed.
No numbers or symbols are drawn on screen; the lockers are plain doors without labels.
The open question is which lockers are open at the end. It is never answered in this video.
video_script.design: One idea: a repeated toggling rule leaves a pattern worth explaining. Assumes nothing. No wrong idea is broken. The row of lockers stays to the end; the photo fades and the drawn row carries on.
